content.value: Primary reading: Rozanski and Woods, Chapter 23. Supplemental: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 architecture description concepts. This unit focuses on cross-view consistency.

Multiple views are useful because no single model can answer every architectural question. The cost is consistency work: names, responsibilities, interfaces, constraints, and assumptions must align across views.
Inconsistency is not always bad. Sometimes a mismatch reveals an unresolved design decision. The important thing is to detect the mismatch and either fix it or record why it is intentional.
Studio: compare a functional view and deployment view, then identify elements that must map cleanly between them.

concepts.name: Cross-view consistency
concepts.description: Alignment among related elements, names, responsibilities, and relationships across architecture views.

concepts.name: View correspondence
concepts.description: A relationship that maps elements or concepts in one view to elements or concepts in another view.

concepts.name: Consistency check
concepts.description: A review activity that searches for contradictions or missing links across architecture artifacts.

concepts.name: Intentional inconsistency
concepts.description: A documented mismatch kept temporarily or deliberately because it reflects migration, variation, or an unresolved decision.
